what: a side file a tool writes itself (scenes/multicam/silence --edl, caption's SRT and ASS, metadata's --chapters-out/--description-out, render's project and pack, verify/report's --report) was written with a plain open()/Path.write_text() after its output check, so a file another process created or edited at that path during the run was overwritten without --overwrite, and an interrupted write left a truncated sidecar
escaped: the replace-time recheck (#470) covered ffmpeg's own outputs and only two files a tool replaces itself (silence.py --timemap, export.py's fill/key); the side-file guards recorded the check but the plain write never compared it again, and no test wrote a sidecar after its check
mechanism: runner.write_sidecar writes an existing caller-named side file in place under the path's output lock and only after refuse_changed_output(), so a file another process put there after the check is refused instead of overwritten and the inode is kept, with its mode, group, access ACL, hard links and any symlink it is; a target the check recorded absent is staged as a hidden sibling temp and installed with os.link() so a file created in the gap is refused instead of replaced, created exclusively and filled when the filesystem has no hard links, and under --overwrite consenting to replace that path; the identity recorded (also in batch.py's report) is the inode this call wrote, not one read back from the path after the install; scenes, multicam, metadata, silence, caption, asr, _ass_overlay, render, report and verify call it instead of a plain open(); silence.py's time map and emit.py's plan use it, and pacing_edit.py's overwrite replace runs under the destination's lock; tests test_a_side_file_written_after_its_check_is_refused_and_one_left_alone_is_written, test_a_side_file_created_between_the_comparison_and_the_install_is_refused, test_an_absent_side_file_that_appears_before_the_install_is_replaced_under_overwrite, test_an_overwrite_pair_puts_back_a_file_that_appeared_at_a_checked_absent_target, test_the_identity_recorded_for_a_side_file_is_the_staged_file_not_a_foreign_one, test_a_side_file_keeps_the_access_acl_of_the_file_it_replaces, test_an_existing_side_file_is_written_in_place_and_keeps_its_links and test_every_side_file_a_tool_writes_itself_goes_through_the_rechecked_helper pin the refusal, the install window, the record, the in-place write and the source sweep
size_reason: the fix measures 108 net Python lines in scripts/ against the merge base (168 added, 60 removed), over fix_max_net_lines (50): the shared writer replaces ten plain open()/write_text() calls across thirteen files and holds the staging, mode, group, identity and install-window logic itself, and trimming it would keep a per-caller write path this change exists to remove. The second review pass adds no net Python line: --overwrite now skips the link install, so a target absent at the check still gives consent to replace whatever is there. The third review pass adds no net Python line either: the paired install keeps the backup for that file under --overwrite, so a failed pair puts back what was there. The fourth review pass added the group keep and its refusal in runner.py, the one reason in _contract.ERROR_REASONS and the doc lines that state it; the review after it asked for the existing target to be written in place instead, which keeps the inode, mode, group, ACL, hard links and symlink by construction and removes that group/ACL keep machinery with both refusal reasons, so the change now measures -102 counted lines in the touched scripts. The fifth review pass adds the exclusive-create install for a filesystem without hard links, the access-ACL copy and its refusal, and the tests and doc lines for both; the fix measures 231 net Python lines against the merge base (295 added, 64 removed), over fix_max_net_lines (50) because this pass alone adds 123: the no-clobber fallback, the ACL copy, and the two refusals are the guarantees the review asked for, and trimming them would leave the old replace or lose named users' permissions.
